title: Inverse image of module sheaves is left adjoint to direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces, $\mathcal A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $Y$, $\mathcal M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules, and $\mathcal N$ a sheaf of $f^{-1}\mathcal A$-modules on $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The inverse-image sheaf $f^{-1}\mathcal M$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] is an $f^{-1}\mathcal A$-module by the inverse image of the action on $\mathcal M$. The direct-image sheaf $f_*\mathcal N$, whose sections over $V\subseteq Y$ are $\mathcal N(f^{-1}V)$, is an $\mathcal A$-module through the unit $\eta_{\mathcal A}:\mathcal A\to f_*f^{-1}\mathcal A$. The inverse-image/direct-image adjunction for abelian sheaves restricts to a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{f^{-1}\mathcal A}(f^{-1}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal M,f_*\mathcal N)$.
